<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Find a lab and its units, reduce repeated readings, present numbers without losing
their meaning, and fit a model that requires an actual follow-up measurement.
</div>

**You need:** [the setup and numeric resource](book-00-start.html), and
[events and reducers](book-06-events.html). Start a fresh session in `book-work`.
This chapter uses synthetic Synthea measurements.


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
```

## Find haemoglobin and its unit


``` r
hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Hemoglobin", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(hits[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept")])
```



| concept_id|concept_name                                                                        |standard_concept |
|----------:|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------|
|    3001643|Hemoglobin and Hematocrit panel - Blood                                             |S                |
|    3004410|Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood                                            |S                |
|   40761014|Hemoglobin.gastrointestinal.lower [Presence] in Stool by Immunoassay --1st specimen |S                |
|    3011397|Hemoglobin [Presence] in Urine by Test strip                                        |S                |
|    3000963|Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood                                                   |S                |

``` r
lab_id <- hits$concept_id[trimws(hits$concept_name) == "Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood"]
units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = lab_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(units[c("value", "concept_name", "n")])
```



|value |concept_name       |   n|
|:-----|:------------------|---:|
|8713  |gram per deciliter | 105|

Choose **3000963**, Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood. The recorded unit is
**8713**, gram per deciliter (g/dL); `value` holds that unit ID, and `n` is a
record count rounded down to a multiple of five. Other haemoglobin concepts
need not measure the same quantity.

## Choose what one person's number means

A unit declaration preserves the chosen unit. With the default unknown-unit
rule, other-unit rows remain but their numeric values become missing; there is
no automatic conversion. First and last use dates, while min and max use magnitude.
All-history mean gives each reading equal weight within a person.


``` r
lab <- omop_event("measurement", concepts = lab_id, unit = omop_unit(8713L))
first <- omop_variable(event = lab, reducer = omop_reduce("first_value"))
last <- omop_variable(event = lab, reducer = omop_reduce("last_value"))
average <- omop_variable(event = lab, reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))
values <- omop_recipe(variables = list(first = first, last = last, mean = average,
  minimum = omop_variable(event = lab, reducer = omop_reduce("min")),
  maximum = omop_variable(event = lab, reducer = omop_reduce("max"))))
invisible(recipe_execute(values, out = "D_labs", conns = conns))
reducer_means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("first", "last", "mean", "minimum", "maximum"), function(column) {
  x <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean(paste0("D_labs$", column), type = "combine", datasources = conns)$Global.Mean
  data.frame(Reducer = column, Mean_g_dl = x[1, "EstimatedMean"],
    Valid = x[1, "Nvalid"], Missing = x[1, "Nmissing"])
}))
knitr::kable(reducer_means, digits = 3)
```



|Reducer | Mean_g_dl| Valid| Missing|
|:-------|---------:|-----:|-------:|
|first   |    13.986|    28|       0|
|last    |    14.893|    28|       0|
|mean    |    14.467|    28|       0|
|minimum |    12.746|    28|       0|
|maximum |    16.104|    28|       0|

The first-value mean is 13.986 g/dL and the last-value mean 14.893 g/dL.
The mean of person means is 14.467 g/dL: each of the 28 people contributes once,
regardless of how many readings they have. Differences between these aggregate
means are not necessarily the average within-person change.

## Keep numbers beside their groups

Grouping first and last values at the same cutoff helps compare distributions.
The count rows describe categories; the last row gives the overall mean once.


``` r
grouped <- omop_recipe(variables = list(first = first, last = last,
  first_group = omop_number_bins(first, breaks = c(-Inf, 14.5, Inf),
    labels = c("below 14.5", "14.5 or above")),
  last_group = omop_number_bins(last, breaks = c(-Inf, 14.5, Inf),
    labels = c("below 14.5", "14.5 or above"))))
invisible(recipe_execute(grouped, out = "D_groups", conns = conns))
comparison <- lapply(c("first", "last"), function(column) {
  counts <- dsBaseClient::ds.table(paste0("D_groups$", column, "_group"), datasources = conns)
  mean <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean(paste0("D_groups$", column), type = "combine", datasources = conns)
  book_group_comparison(counts, mean, column, "g/dL")
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, comparison), digits = 3)
```



|Category             | Count|Number |Unit | Overall mean|
|:--------------------|-----:|:------|:----|------------:|
|below 14.5           |    16|first  |g/dL |           NA|
|14.5 or above        |    12|first  |g/dL |           NA|
|NA                   |     0|first  |g/dL |           NA|
|Overall (all groups) |    NA|first  |g/dL |       13.986|
|below 14.5           |    10|last   |g/dL |           NA|
|14.5 or above        |    18|last   |g/dL |           NA|
|NA                   |     0|last   |g/dL |           NA|
|Overall (all groups) |    NA|last   |g/dL |       14.893|

Read the category counts to see how many first or last values fall on each side
of 14.5. The overall means describe all 28 people, not the people in an individual category.
These cutoffs illustrate presentation; they are not clinical reference limits.

## Select a nearby value and measure change

Index seven days after first haemoglobin and look back seven days. Everyone has
a reading in that window by construction; the nearest reading can still differ
from the first.


``` r
indexed <- omop_study(omop_index(lab, offset = 7L), outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(at_index = omop_value_at_index("measurement", lab_id,
    tolerance = c(-7, 0), unit = omop_unit(8713L))))
invisible(recipe_execute(indexed, out = c(baseline = "D_index"), conns = conns))
knitr::kable(book_summary("D_index$at_index", datasources = conns))
```



|Site |Statistic |  Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | 11.810|      28|         0|
|site |10%       | 12.480|      28|         0|
|site |25%       | 12.975|      28|         0|
|site |50%       | 13.700|      28|         0|
|site |75%       | 15.425|      28|         0|
|site |90%       | 16.190|      28|         0|
|site |95%       | 16.855|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      | 14.150|      28|         0|

All 28 values are present. The mean becomes 14.150 g/dL because one person's
next-day reading, 11.6, replaces their first reading, 7.0. Those values belong to
the public synthetic example; in a study, the protected summary alone would not
identify the changed person. A narrower tolerance could leave missing values.

A slope fits value against actual date within each person. Difference is last
minus first; percent and ratio additionally divide by first. A zero baseline
cannot support those divisions. Two eligible readings are required for change,
and a slope needs distinct dates.


``` r
changes <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  change = omop_number_change(lab, "difference"),
  percent = omop_number_change(lab, "percent_change"),
  ratio = omop_number_change(lab, "ratio"),
  per_year = omop_number(omop_number_change(lab, "slope", time_unit = "days"),
    omop_number_spec(transform = omop_number_transform("affine", factor = 365))),
  target_days = omop_number_change(lab, "time_to_threshold", threshold = 14,
    op = "ge", reference = "first", time_unit = "days")))
invisible(recipe_execute(changes, out = "D_change", conns = conns))
knitr::kable(book_summary("D_change$change", datasources = conns))
```



|Site |Statistic |  Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | -2.940|      25|         3|
|site |10%       | -2.580|      25|         3|
|site |25%       | -1.400|      25|         3|
|site |50%       |  1.600|      25|         3|
|site |75%       |  2.400|      25|         3|
|site |90%       |  3.200|      25|         3|
|site |95%       |  3.760|      25|         3|
|site |Mean      |  1.016|      25|         3|

``` r
knitr::kable(book_summary("D_change$per_year", datasources = conns))
```



|Site |Statistic |      Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|----------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | -0.2631522|      25|         3|
|site |10%       | -0.2238866|      25|         3|
|site |25%       | -0.0506511|      25|         3|
|site |50%       |  0.0806739|      25|         3|
|site |75%       |  0.1515094|      25|         3|
|site |90%       |  0.2860863|      25|         3|
|site |95%       |  0.4025790|      25|         3|
|site |Mean      |  0.0521556|      25|         3|

There are 25 valid changes and three missing: single-reading people do not have
observed change. Mean change is 1.016 g/dL. The median slope is about 0.081 g/dL
per 365 days. Neither statistic implies the same change for every person, and a
linear slope does not forecast a person's next reading.

## Convert, round and classify in a declared order

Target unit **8636** is gram per liter (g/L), found in [chapter 6](book-06-events.html#convert-to-a-common-unit-before-reducing). Multiplication
by ten converts g/dL to g/L. Here the conversion is applied to the person mean;
an event-level `omop_unit(8636L, convert = list("8713" = c(factor = 10, offset = 0)))`
would convert before reduction instead.


``` r
band_labels <- c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above")
presentation <- omop_number_pipeline(
  omop_number_unit("unit:8713", "unit:8636", factor = 10),
  omop_number_round("decimals", 1),
  omop_number_spec(representation = "bins", breaks = c(0, 140, 150, 1000),
    labels = c("below 140", "140 to below 150", "150 or above")))
flags <- omop_recipe(variables = list(mean = average,
  rounded = omop_number(average, omop_number_spec(rounding = omop_number_round("decimals", 1))),
  band = omop_number_bins(average, breaks = c(-Inf, 14, 15, Inf), labels = band_labels),
  converted_band = omop_number(average, presentation),
  control = omop_number_category(average, range = "thresholds", thresholds = c(14, 15)),
  high = omop_number_flag(average, "ge", 15)))
invisible(recipe_execute(flags, out = "D_flags", conns = conns))
knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_flags$band", datasources = conns)))
```



|Category       | Count|
|:--------------|-----:|
|below 14       |     9|
|14 to below 15 |     9|
|15 or above    |    10|
|NA             |     0|

``` r
knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_flags$converted_band", datasources = conns)))
```



|Category         | Count|
|:----------------|-----:|
|below 140        |     9|
|140 to below 150 |     9|
|150 or above     |    10|
|NA               |     0|

Both presentations give category counts 9, 9 and 10 here. Bins are left-closed:
14 belongs to the middle bin and 15 to the upper bin. The factor is ordered;
polynomial contrasts change coefficient interpretation, but a full set of those
contrasts gives the same fit as a full set of dummy variables.

The equal counts do not mean rounding can never change a category. Consider a
public example near the boundary:


``` r
x <- 13.996
knitr::kable(data.frame(Input_g_dl = x, Converted_g_l = 10 * x,
  Rounded_g_l = round(10 * x, 1), Before = "below 140", After = "140 to below 150"))
```



| Input_g_dl| Converted_g_l| Rounded_g_l|Before    |After            |
|----------:|-------------:|-----------:|:---------|:----------------|
|     13.996|        139.96|         140|below 140 |140 to below 150 |

139.96 rounds to 140.0 and crosses the cutoff. Rounding uses ties-to-even;
classifying before rounding would answer a different question.


``` r
knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_flags$control", datasources = conns)))
```



|Category | Count|
|:--------|-----:|
|low      |     9|
|normal   |     9|
|high     |    10|
|NA       |     0|

``` r
knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_flags$high", datasources = conns)))
```



|Category | Count|
|:--------|-----:|
|0        |    18|
|1        |    10|
|NA       |     0|

The high flag is one for 10 people. The category thresholds define low <14,
normal 14–15 **inclusive**, and high >15, whereas the flag uses ≥15. Thus a value
exactly 15 would be normal in the category but high in the flag.
Synthea has no haemoglobin reference bounds; missing bounds cannot establish normality.

## Fit a model only for people with follow-up

A last value equal to first because no second reading exists is not a follow-up
outcome. Index on the first lab and restrict last to days 1 onward. Use two
disjoint practice sites; their combined population is the same 28 people.
The named `paired` session keeps the earlier single-site tables available for
the exercises below.

For real servers, replace the next two connection lines with the
[two-site Opal login](book-00-start.html#connect-to-two-opal-sites).
Keep the earlier `conns` connection for the later single-site exercises.


``` r
practice_pair <- book_connect("numeric", two_sites = TRUE, symbol = "book_pool", session = "paired")
two_conns <- practice_pair$conns
followup <- omop_study(lab, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  first = omop_value_at_index("measurement", lab_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8713L)),
  last = omop_variable(event = lab, reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", window = omop_window(1, NULL))),
  mean = average))
invisible(recipe_execute(followup, out = c(baseline = "D_pool"), conns = two_conns, symbol = "book_pool"))
pooled_mean <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_pool$mean", type = "combine", datasources = two_conns)$Global.Mean
knitr::kable(pooled_mean, digits = 3)
```



|                | EstimatedMean| Nmissing| Nvalid| Ntotal|
|:---------------|-------------:|--------:|------:|------:|
|studiesCombined |        14.467|        0|     28|     28|

The pooled mean remains 14.467 g/dL across 28 people. Each nonmissing person
receives equal weight; opening two connections to the same people would double-count them.


``` r
quantiles <- dsBaseClient::ds.quantileMean("D_pool$mean", type = "combine", datasources = two_conns)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Statistic = names(quantiles), Value = as.numeric(quantiles)), digits = 3)
```



|Statistic |  Value|
|:---------|------:|
|5%        | 13.020|
|10%       | 13.290|
|25%       | 13.851|
|50%       | 14.289|
|75%       | 15.306|
|90%       | 15.725|
|95%       | 15.910|
|Mean      | 14.467|

These are weighted averages of site quantiles, not exact quantiles of all people
combined. The mean always agrees with the pooled mean because this function
weights site means by their nonmissing N.

dsBase's local steps may warn; check `$iter` and the final errors for convergence.
The model below relates last to first haemoglobin only among the 25 people with
a later reading; their follow-up ranges from one day to about 18 years.


``` r
fit <- dsBaseClient::ds.glm("last ~ first", data = "D_pool", family = "gaussian", datasources = two_conns)
b <- fit$coefficients["first", "Estimate"]
se <- fit$coefficients["first", "Std. Error"]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Estimate = b, Lower_95 = b - qt(.975, 23) * se,
  Upper_95 = b + qt(.975, 23) * se), digits = 3)
```



| Estimate| Lower_95| Upper_95|
|--------:|--------:|--------:|
|   -0.159|   -0.454|    0.136|

The slope is about −0.159: a 1 g/dL higher first reading is associated with a
0.159 g/dL lower last reading in this small sample. Its 95% t interval, −0.454 to 0.136, includes zero. Variable follow-up and regression to the mean limit this
comparison; it is not an effect of treatment or a common-time trajectory.

## Exercises

**1. Transform a person mean.** Calculate log(mean haemoglobin). Is this the mean
of that person's logged readings?

<details><summary>Solution 1</summary>


``` r
logged <- omop_recipe(variables = list(log_mean = omop_number(average,
  omop_number_spec(transform = omop_number_transform("log")))))
invisible(recipe_execute(logged, out = "D_log", conns = conns))
knitr::kable(book_summary("D_log$log_mean", datasources = conns))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|--------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | 2.557554|      28|         0|
|site |10%       | 2.576166|      28|         0|
|site |25%       | 2.623579|      28|         0|
|site |50%       | 2.661968|      28|         0|
|site |75%       | 2.730164|      28|         0|
|site |90%       | 2.753634|      28|         0|
|site |95%       | 2.767809|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      | 2.669345|      28|         0|

The median is about 2.662, the log of the median person mean, 14.325.
Reduction precedes the transform: log of a mean generally differs from mean of logs.

</details>

**2. Interpret observed attainment.** Summarise days until the first observed
haemoglobin ≥14. How do zero and missing differ?

<details><summary>Solution 2</summary>


``` r
knitr::kable(book_summary("D_change$target_days", datasources = conns))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|--------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        |    0.000|      26|         2|
|site |10%       |    0.000|      26|         2|
|site |25%       |    0.000|      26|         2|
|site |50%       |  185.500|      26|         2|
|site |75%       | 2192.750|      26|         2|
|site |90%       | 3052.000|      26|         2|
|site |95%       | 4166.750|      26|         2|
|site |Mean      | 1274.808|      26|         2|

There are 26 observed attainments and two missing; median time among observed
attainments is 185.5 days. Zero means the first reading already meets the rule. Missing means no qualifying
reading was observed; use follow-up and censoring for a time-to-event analysis
rather than replacing missing with zero or discarding those people.

</details>

**3. Keep a rounded copy beside the original.** Request the copy from the output
and summarise it. Must its overall mean have one decimal place?

<details><summary>Solution 3</summary>


``` r
copy <- omop_recipe(variables = list(mean = average),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", columns = c("mean", "rounded"),
    number_columns = list(rounded = omop_number_column("mean",
      number_spec = omop_number_spec(rounding = omop_number_round("decimals", 1))))))
invisible(recipe_execute(copy, out = "D_copy", conns = conns))
knitr::kable(book_summary("D_copy$rounded", datasources = conns))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|--------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | 12.90500|      28|         0|
|site |10%       | 13.17000|      28|         0|
|site |25%       | 13.77500|      28|         0|
|site |50%       | 14.30000|      28|         0|
|site |75%       | 15.32500|      28|         0|
|site |90%       | 15.69000|      28|         0|
|site |95%       | 15.96500|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      | 14.45714|      28|         0|

The overall rounded mean is 14.457 g/dL. Each person's copy has one decimal, but averaging those values can produce more
decimals. The original mean remains available for analysis; rounding does not
add measurement precision.

</details>

## Recap

Define the lab, unit, time window and person-level reducer before interpreting a
number. Preserve missing follow-up, state threshold boundaries, and distinguish
site-quantile averages from pooled person-level estimates.
